title: Sticking to the wall: the gecko's secret
text: A gecko can sprint up polished glass {{1}} any glue, suction or claws. The secret sits on its toes, which are covered {{2}} millions of microscopic hairs, each branching into hundreds of finer tips. Each tip sits {{3}} close to the surface that weak intermolecular attractions begin to act, and across billions of tips they become {{4}} to support the animal's whole weight many times over. As it runs, the gecko peels each toe {{5}} at a shallow angle, breaking the bonds instantly and leaving {{6}} residue behind, so the foot never loses its grip. Engineers have now built the principle {{7}} reusable adhesives and climbing robots, and, remarkably, a gecko's foot even cleans {{8}} between steps.

gaps.explanation: 'Without' expresses the absence of the usual aids.

gaps.hint: adverb: ___ close to the surface that
adverb: become ___ to support the weight
gaps.explanation: 'Adjective + enough + to' — sufficient degree for the result.
'Peel off' — the particle shows separation from the surface.
The foot acts on itself: it cleans itself.
